nodes.description: Melanocytes isolated from a café-au-lait macule of an affected individual carried, in addition to the germline SPRED1 variant, an acquired somatic mutation in the wild-type SPRED1 allele. Café-au-lait macule formation in Legius syndrome therefore follows a two-hit, mosaic-somatic logic in the melanocyte lineage, mirroring the second-hit requirement described for NF1 pigmentary lesions, rather than arising from germline haploinsufficiency alone.

nodes.description: The cardinal and often sole objective finding of Legius syndrome: multiple, bilaterally distributed café-au-lait macules, with or without skinfold (axillary or inguinal) freckling, clinically indistinguishable from those of neurofibromatosis type 1. Because the pigmentary phenotype is shared, roughly half of individuals with a SPRED1 variant satisfy the older NIH clinical criteria for NF1 despite having a different natural history — the observation that drove the 2021 consensus revision to make a molecular SPRED1 result a required diagnostic criterion.

evidence.snippet: LGSS, inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern, is characterized by multiple CALMs similar to NF1 with or without skinfold freckling, caused by heterozygous PVs in SPRED1, located on chromosome 15.

nodes.description: Legius syndrome is caused by heterozygous germline loss-of-function variants in SPRED1, a member of the SPROUTY/SPRED family of proteins that act as negative regulators of the RAS-RAF interaction and downstream MAPK signaling. This was the first human disease attributed to the SPRY/SPRED gene family and placed the disorder within the RASopathy group of RAS-MAPK pathway disorders.

evidence.snippet: We report germline loss-of-function mutations in SPRED1 in a newly identified autosomal dominant human disorder. SPRED1 is a member of the SPROUTY/SPRED family of proteins that act as negative regulators of RAS->RAF interaction and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling.

evidence.reference_title: Spred is a Sprouty-related suppressor of Ras signalling.
evidence.snippet: Like Sprouty, Spred inhibited growth-factor-mediated activation of MAP kinase.

nodes.description: Spred1-null mice show impaired performance in the Morris water maze and visual-discrimination T-maze with normal basic neuromotor and sensory abilities, together with defects in short- and long-term hippocampal synaptic plasticity including a disequilibrium between long-term potentiation and long-term depression in CA1. Increased ERK phosphorylation is measurable in Spred1-null slices after LTP induction, linking the plasticity defect to Ras/ERK hyperactivation. This is the candidate substrate for the learning disability, ADHD, and developmental delay reported in affected individuals, but the translational step from mouse hippocampal physiology to the human cognitive phenotype has not been directly demonstrated (see the HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH discussion).

evidence.reference_title: Spred1 is required for synaptic plasticity and hippocampus-dependent learning.
evidence.snippet: Electrophysiological recordings on brain slices from these animals identified defects in short- and long-term synaptic hippocampal plasticity, including a disequilibrium between long-term potentiation (LTP) and long-term depression in CA1 region.

evidence.reference_title: Spred1 is required for synaptic plasticity and hippocampus-dependent learning.
evidence.snippet: Spred1(-/-) mice show decreased learning and memory performance in the Morris water maze and visual-discrimination T-maze, but normal basic neuromotor and sensory abilities.

nodes.description: SPRED1 suppresses RAS-ERK signaling not by acting on RAS directly but by serving as a membrane-targeting adaptor for neurofibromin, the RAS-GAP encoded by NF1. The SPRED1 EVH1 domain binds short N- and C-terminal helical extensions flanking the GAP-related domain (GRD) of neurofibromin — regions dispensable for GAP catalysis and absent from p120GAP, which explains the selectivity of SPRED1 for neurofibromin among RasGAPs. Pathogenic EVH1-domain missense variants found in Legius syndrome reduce GRD binding affinity and correspondingly abolish the ERK-suppressing activity of SPRED1, providing a direct molecular link between genotype and pathway dysregulation. Structural work confirms that SPRED1-mediated membrane targeting allows neurofibromin to engage activated KRAS simultaneously.

nodes.description: Like the other RASopathies, Legius syndrome results from germline dysregulation of the RAS-MAPK (RAS/ERK) signal transduction cascade. The shared pathway lesion places the disorder in the same phenotypically overlapping family as neurofibromatosis type 1, Noonan syndrome, Costello syndrome, and cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome, and accounts for the macrocephaly, pigmentary, and neurocognitive features shared across the group. In Legius syndrome the dysregulation is comparatively mild and does not reach the threshold required for neurofibroma or other NF1 tumor formation.

evidence.reference_title: Germline loss-of-function mutations in SPRED1 cause a neurofibromatosis 1-like phenotype.
evidence.snippet: This disorder is yet another member of the recently characterized group of phenotypically overlapping syndromes caused by mutations in the genes encoding key components of the RAS-MAPK pathway.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and mutational spectrum of neurofibromatosis type 1-like syndrome.
evidence.snippet: In the anonymous cohort of 1318 individuals, 34 different SPRED1 mutations in 43 probands were identified: 27 pathogenic mutations in 34 probands and 7 probable nonpathogenic missense mutations in 9 probands.

evidence.reference_title: Revised diagnostic criteria for neurofibromatosis type 1 and Legius syndrome: an international consensus recommendation.
evidence.snippet: Further studies have shown that SPRED1 PVs account for 1% of sporadic cases and 19% of familial cases with pigmentary features of NF1 (CALMs and freckling) only.

evidence.reference_title: SPRED1 germline mutations caused a neurofibromatosis type 1 overlapping phenotype.
evidence.snippet: Germline loss-of-function mutations in the SPRED1 gene have recently been identified in patients fulfilling the National Institutes of Health (NIH) diagnostic criteria for neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) but with no NF1 (neurofibromin 1) mutation found, suggesting a neurofibromatosis type 1-like syndrome.
